Affable

AF-uh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Affable is friendly, warm, and easy to approach or talk to.

Despite being one of the most decorated scientists at the conference, Dr. Reyes was so affable that first-year graduate students felt comfortable striking up conversations with her at lunch.

Worked Example

The new librarian's affable manner -- always ready with a smile and a book recommendation -- made even reluctant readers want to stop by the front desk.

Affable describes an easygoing warmth in how someone interacts with others -- it's about pleasant, approachable manner, not necessarily deep friendship.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

amiable: friendly and pleasant, easy to like

congenial: pleasant and agreeable, easy to get along with

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

aloof: distant and uninvolved; not friendly or approachable

surly: bad-tempered and unfriendly

Where it sits · how warmly they welcome company — polite → affable → gregarious

polite vs. affable: Polite just means basic courtesy -- it can be a bit formal or distant, without the genuine warmth of being affable.

gregarious vs. affable: Gregarious goes even further than affable, describing someone who actively seeks out company rather than simply being pleasant when approached.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — af-

prefix — af-: variant of ad-, 'to, toward' (Latin)

root — fa-

root — fa-: to speak (Latin fari)

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: able to be (Latin -abilis)

Put it together

Put it together: Affable comes from Latin ad- ('toward') + fari ('to speak') -- literally 'easy to speak to.' That same fari root also hides inside this unit's own ineffable ('unable to be spoken'), and inside the everyday word fable ('a thing spoken or told'). Three words, one ancient root about speaking.

Use the root in a new word: fable

Use the root in a new word: fable: The old fable about the tortoise and the hare still teaches the same lesson centuries later.
